output.name: Skenal
output.myth: When the herring failed, a boat went out past the Leeward edge with her name in old red paint on the stern. The sea took the paint before it took the boat. When the crew came home without her, the mothers scraped the name from the broken hull and burned the wood, so it would not be called. But a boat with no name cannot find its way home, and a lantern that cannot say what it is will hang wherever it is put. So it went looking. Aun saw it first, too low over the water. Ennu laughed and said it was welcome to any name it liked. Its red is the red of the kite Tiru's mother flew from the cliff, and the lantern hangs a fist and a half west of that kite. To the north-east the women keep an iron kettle on the hearth for the boat that did not come back, and nobody sits by it. Kael casts for it and never catches it; the light sits just above the rope. Sil watches it while she hunts her brother. If a lamp hangs too still past the reef, do not shout. Ask it, quietly, what it was called.
output.finding: Find the Red Kite, Tiru, low in the Leeward Reach, then look a fist and a half west of it, where the lantern hangs too still above the water.
